newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EU's Kinnock sees transport paralysis ahead.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock sees transport paralysis ahead.

text.p: European Union transport commissioner Neil Kinnock on Thursday said European cities were heading towards "commercial thrombosis" unless action was taken to improve public transport and reduce car use.
"Substantial change is absolutely essential. In the absence of such change, increased pollution, congestion and accidents are guaranteed," he told a business forum in the Austrian capital.
But transport decisions had to be taken at a local and national level and the European Commission could only provide guidelines for improvement, he said.
Kinnock said passenger traffic in the European Union had grown around 3.2 percent annually in the last 25 years and car travel had soared by 120 percent.
He predicted that in 10 years, 600 people in every 1,000 would own cars, compared with 435 in every 1,000 at present.
